'''Neem Chandra Bhowmik''' ({{langx|bn|নিমচন্দ্র ভৌমিক}}; died 4 October 2026) was a Bangladeshi physicist and diplomat who was a professor in the Department of Applied Physics at the [[University of Dhaka]] and a leader of the [[Hinduism in Bangladesh|Hindu minority community in Bangladesh]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Minority leader named as Diplomat |url=https://www.modernghana.com/news/227231/minority-leader-named-as-diplomat.html |access-date=2022-03-29 |work=ModernGhana |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Minority bodies announce weeklong demo seeking election deferment |url=https://unb.com.bd/category/Bangladesh/minority-bodies-announce-weeklong-demo-seeking-election-deferment/41618 |access-date=2022-03-29 |work=UNB |language=en}}</ref> He was the Ambassador of [[Bangladesh–Nepal relations|Bangladesh to Nepal]] with a controversial term.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Be united to keep Bangladesh-India friendship unharmed: Abdur Razzak {{!}} News |url=https://www.bssnews.net/news/34301 |access-date=2022-03-29 |work=BSS}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2011-10-30 |title=Bangladesh sending investigators to Nepal |url=https://www.timesofassam.com/international/bangladesh-sending-investigators-to-nepal/ |access-date=2022-03-29 |work=Times of Assam |language=en-US |archive-date=11 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220811181406/https://www.timesofassam.com/international/bangladesh-sending-investigators-to-nepal/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was the president of Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Representative of minorities in EC sought |url=https://www.newagebd.net/article/162745/representative-of-minorities-in-ec-sought |access-date=2022-03-29 |work=New Age |language=en}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
In 2007, while Bhowmik was the Chairperson of the Department of Applied Physics at [[University of Dhaka|Dhaka University]], he was arrested during student protests under the military-backed [[Caretaker government of Bangladesh|caretaker government]].<ref>{{Cite news |script-title=bn:নিমচন্দ্রের কেলেঙ্কারি: ঢাকা ফিরেছে তদন্ত দল |url=https://bangla.bdnews24.com/bangladesh/article481979.bdnews |access-date=2024-09-09 |work=bdnews24.com |language=bn}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2020-08-23 |title=DU teachers and students observe Black Day |url=https://archive.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/dhaka/2020/08/23/du-teachers-and-students-observe-black-day |access-date=2022-03-29 |work=Dhaka Tribune}}</ref><ref name=":02">{{Cite news |date=2007-09-19 |title=Prof Neem sent to jail on surrender |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-4596 |access-date=2022-03-29 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref> In March 2008, the court declared him innocent.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2008-03-19 |title=4 DU students appeal against conviction |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-28461 |access-date=2022-03-29 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref>

On 22 July 2009, the Bangladesh appointed Bhowmik Ambassador of Bangladesh to Nepal.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |title=Neem Bhowmik new envoy to Nepal |url=https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2009/07/22/neem-bhowmik-new-envoy-to-nepal |access-date=2022-03-29 |work=bdnews24.com |archive-date=29 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220329054219/https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2009/07/22/neem-bhowmik-new-envoy-to-nepal |url-status=dead }}</ref> In July 2010, Bhowmik was awarded the Mother Teresa Gold Medal.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2010-07-22 |title=20 receive Mother Teresa Gold Medal |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-147800 |access-date=2022-03-29 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref>

In July 2011, Nepal requested the withdrawal of Bhowmik from his post in Nepal. A [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Bangladesh)|Bangladeshi Foreign Ministry]] report accused Bhowmik of professional misconduct, violating diplomatic norms, and involvement in Nepalese politics. He was also accused of accepting kickbacks from Nepali students for scholarships, stalking actress [[Manisha Koirala]], and harassing Indian Embassy spokeswoman Mrs. Apoorva Srivastava. Additionally, he used an embassy car inappropriately and made controversial remarks at a Mujibnagar anniversary event. Complaints about his behavior towards women were also raised.<ref name=":22">{{Cite news |title=Nepal wants Bangladesh envoy recalled |url=https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2011/07/18/nepal-wants-bangladesh-envoy-recalled |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220329054108/https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2011/07/18/nepal-wants-bangladesh-envoy-recalled |archive-date=29 March 2022 |access-date=2022-03-29 |work=bdnews24.com}}</ref> The government decided not to extend his ambassadorship.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Karim |first=Rezaul |date=2012-06-30 |title=Major changes in foreign office |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-240381 |access-date=2022-03-29 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref> A committee was formed to review the allegations,<ref>{{Cite news |date=2011-07-19 |title=Probe body to check allegations |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-194791 |access-date=2022-03-29 |work=The Daily Star |language=en}}</ref> and if no serious findings were reported, he would be granted a respectful exit.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2011-11-17 |script-title=bn:ক্ষমা পাচ্ছেন রাষ্ট্রদূত নিমচন্দ্র ভৌমিক |url=https://www.banglanews24.com/national/news/bd/69067.details |access-date=2024-09-09 |work=banglanews24.com |language=bn}}</ref>

== Leadership roles ==
Bhowmik was the general secretary of [[Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council]] multiple times.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Refugees |first=United Nations High Commissioner for |title=Refworld {{!}} Bangladesh: Information on the Bangladesh, Hindu, Buddhist and Christian Unity Council (Bangladesh, Hindu, Buddhist Christian Oihya Parishad); on the name of the general secretary; and on whether the organization issues membership letters to individuals who have left the country |url=https://www.refworld.org/docid/3ae6ab8844.html |access-date=2022-03-29 |website=Refworld |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":12" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Pintu |first=Rafiqul Islam |title=Dr NC Bhowmik president, Rana Dasgupta secretary |url=http://dailyasianage.com/news/279642/?regenerate |access-date=2022-03-29 |work=The Asian Age |language=en}}</ref> He was also the president of Bangladesh Muktijodha Foundation and Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad.<ref name=":12">{{Cite news |title=Neem Bhowmik new envoy to Nepal |url=https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2009/07/22/neem-bhowmik-new-envoy-to-nepal |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220329054219/https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2009/07/22/neem-bhowmik-new-envoy-to-nepal |archive-date=29 March 2022 |access-date=2022-03-29 |work=bdnews24.com}}</ref> 

== Death ==
Bhowmik died at a hospital in [[Dhaka]] on 4 October 2026.<ref>{{cite news |title=Prof Neem Chandra Bhowmik passes away |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/news/news/prof-neem-chandra-bhowmik-passes-away-4290016 |access-date=4 October 2026 |publisher=The Daily Star |date=4 October 2026}}</ref>
